gerund noun

also gerunds, verbal noun, gerundive

late Latin

Diom. p. 350 P.; Prisc. p. 808 P. (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 234, 246, 320

gerundium, gerundiī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a gerund

A term of the later grammarians; Lewis & Short cites Servius calling it gerundīvus modus. A verbal noun with only the oblique cases: legendī librōs causā, for the sake of reading books (Traupman 234); it has no nominative, gerundium eget cāsū nōminātīvō (241).

Other words

  • gerundīvum, gerundīvī n. — gerundive

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 320 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • Gerundium quid est? — Est nōmen verbāle.

    What is a gerund? — It is a verbal noun.Traupman 234

See also participle, gerundive, verb.
